description: Remove the WebGL/R3F 3D hero background animation entirely and leave the home hero intentional and polished using the existing hero video + static aurora backdrop. Delete the three/ component tree, purge the three/@react-three deps, remove now-dead CSS, and revert the WebGL-only CSP/img-src blob: allowance if nothing else uses blob URLs. The user strongly dislikes the 3D background, so it must be fully gone (no lazy-loaded WebGL, no three code in the bundle) while the hero must NOT become empty or broken.
steps: In src/routes/index.tsx: remove `import { ClientCanvas } from "@/components/three/client-canvas";` and the `<ClientCanvas className="home-hero-canvas" fallback={<div className="home-hero-canvas-fallback" ... />} />` element from the .immersive-hero-section. Keep the `.aurora-mesh-container` aurora blobs, the `.hero-copy` block, and the `.hero-perspective-stage` with `<HeroVideo poster={robotsPoster} mp4={robotsVideo} />` intact so the hero remains a polished video + aurora composition. Keep the `import { HeroVideo }` and the two asset imports. Verify the hero still has a full visual backdrop (the aurora mesh) after ClientCanvas is gone so it does not look empty.

In src/components/site-shell.tsx: remove `import { HeroCanvas } from "@/components/three/hero-canvas";` and remove the now-unused `ImmersiveHero` export (it is the only consumer of HeroCanvas and is not referenced anywhere else in src - confirm with `git grep -n ImmersiveHero src` returning no other usage before deleting). Leave PageIntro, PageLayout, SiteHeader, SiteFooter, Brand untouched.

Delete the three component files: src/components/three/hero-scene.tsx, src/components/three/client-canvas.tsx, src/components/three/hero-canvas.tsx, and the now-empty src/components/three/ directory. Before deleting, run `git grep -n "components/three\|HeroScene\|ClientCanvas\|HeroCanvas"` across src to confirm no remaining importers.

In src/lib/motion.ts: the WebGL layer is gone, but motion.test.ts (@vitest-environment node) imports and asserts BOTH `prefersReducedMotion` and `supportsWebGL`. DO NOT remove those two exports or change their SSR-safe return contract (prefersReducedMotion()->false, supportsWebGL()->false without a DOM). `useHasMounted`/`useIsMounted`/`useReducedMotion` are still used by smooth-scroll.tsx and marquee.tsx, so keep them too. Net: motion.ts is unchanged unless a dead helper exists that nothing imports - do not remove supportsWebGL even though its only prior caller (client-canvas) is deleted, because the test pins it.

In package.json dependencies: remove `@react-three/drei`, `@react-three/fiber`, `three`. In devDependencies: remove `@types/three`. Leave `lenis` and everything else. Do NOT run npm install and do NOT edit package-lock.json (it is already stale and cannot be regenerated in this sandbox; the deploy/CI use `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` which reconciles it). Note: removing three also removes the reason react/react-dom were pinned to ~19.2 (that pin satisfied @react-three/fiber's peer range per commit 484def9) - LEAVE the ~19.2 pins as-is to avoid churn and keep the lockfile workaround stable; do not widen them.

In src/styles.css: remove the now-dead WebGL-canvas CSS that no markup references anymore: `.immersive-canvas-layer`, `.immersive-canvas-layer canvas, .immersive-canvas-inner`, `.immersive-hero-section > .hero-perspective-stage` canvas-specific rule only if it is canvas-specific (keep the z-index lift for .hero-copy/.hero-perspective-stage), `.immersive-canvas-layer.home-hero-canvas`, `.home-hero-canvas-fallback`, and the entire dedicated `.immersive-hero`/`.immersive-hero-canvas`/`.immersive-hero-canvas .immersive-canvas-layer`/`.immersive-hero-overlay` block (that styled the deleted ImmersiveHero component). KEEP `.immersive-hero-section` (still used by index.tsx) and its `> .hero-copy, > .hero-perspective-stage { position: relative; z-index: 1 }` rule. KEEP the reduced-motion guard block and the immersive-cursor/marquee/magnetic styles (those primitives remain). Do not touch aurora, film-grain, site-atmosphere, or hero-perspective styles.

In src/server.ts CSP: the `img-src 'self' data: blob:` blob: source and the `worker-src 'self' blob:` blob: source were added specifically for WebGL (canvas readback + drei/draco workers). With the R3F scene removed, confirm via `git grep -n "createObjectURL\|toBlob\|new Blob\|Worker(\|new Worker\|blob:" src` that no remaining client code creates blob: URLs or workers. If none remain, revert `img-src` to `"img-src 'self' data:"`. For worker-src: Vite's dev client / TanStack Router devtools still spawn blob: workers per the existing comment, so KEEP `worker-src 'self' blob:` to avoid breaking dev HMR/devtools. Update the CSP comments to remove references to the WebGL layer (three/@react-three/drei/draco) and explain the remaining blob: worker-src is for the Vite dev client only. Leave all other headers unchanged.

Update the CSP explanatory comment block near the top of src/server.ts so it no longer claims an 'immersive 3D layer (three + @react-three/fiber + @react-three/drei)' is bundled; describe the current same-origin video/CSS/lenis reality instead.
acceptance_criteria: No file under src imports `three`, `@react-three/fiber`, or `@react-three/drei` (verify: `git grep -n "@react-three\|from \"three\"\|from 'three'"` in src returns nothing).
src/components/three/ directory no longer exists and nothing imports components/three/* (verify: `git grep -n "components/three"` returns nothing).
package.json no longer lists three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, or @types/three.
The home hero (index.tsx .immersive-hero-section) still renders the aurora mesh, hero copy, and HeroVideo perspective card, with no ClientCanvas and no empty/blank backdrop layer left dangling.
src/lib/motion.ts still exports prefersReducedMotion and supportsWebGL with unchanged SSR-safe behavior (so motion.test.ts still passes by reasoning).
No dangling CSS selectors reference a canvas/ImmersiveHero that no longer exists, and `.immersive-hero-section` styling for hero-copy/hero-perspective-stage is preserved.
server.ts CSP: img-src reverted to `'self' data:` if no blob: image usage remains; worker-src blob: kept for the Vite dev client; comments updated to drop 3D-layer references.
Reduced-motion CSS guard block and the immersive-cursor/marquee/magnetic styles remain intact.
verification: Run `git grep -n "@react-three\|components/three\|HeroScene\|from \"three\"" src` and confirm zero matches (dead-reference check).
Run `git grep -n "ImmersiveHero\|HeroCanvas\|ClientCanvas" src` and confirm zero matches.
Run `git grep -n "home-hero-canvas\|immersive-canvas-layer\|immersive-hero-canvas\|immersive-hero-overlay" src` and confirm zero matches (dead CSS/markup removed).

Authoritative: CI must pass `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build` on node 22 with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`. Reason through types (no imports of removed modules; index.tsx and site-shell.tsx still type-check) since these cannot run in-sandbox.
findings: Removed the WebGL/R3F 3D hero background entirely. Changes: (1) src/routes/index.tsx - dropped the ClientCanvas import + <ClientCanvas> element and its fallback div; hero now renders aurora-mesh-container + hero-copy + hero-perspective-stage (<HeroVideo>), a full non-empty backdrop (aurora CSS at styles.css ~2112 is intact). (2) src/components/site-shell.tsx - removed HeroCanvas import and the unused ImmersiveHero export (git grep confirmed ImmersiveHero had no other consumer); ReactNode still used by PageLayout/PageIntro. (3) Deleted src/components/three/{hero-scene,client-canvas,hero-canvas}.tsx via git rm; directory is gone. (4) src/lib/motion.ts UNCHANGED - prefersReducedMotion + supportsWebGL exports preserved with SSR-safe contract so motion.test.ts still passes. (5) package.json - removed deps @react-three/drei, @react-three/fiber, three and devDep @types/three; left lenis and react/react-dom pinned at ~19.2 (did NOT widen). (6) src/styles.css - removed dead .immersive-canvas-layer (+ canvas/.immersive-canvas-inner), .immersive-canvas-layer.home-hero-canvas, .home-hero-canvas-fallback, and the whole .immersive-hero/.immersive-hero-canvas/.immersive-hero-overlay block; also removed the now-unused --z-canvas token and de-3D'd its comment. KEPT .immersive-hero-section + its hero-copy/hero-perspective-stage z-index rule, the reduced-motion guard block (updated its comment to drop the WebGL-canvas reference), and all immersive-cursor/marquee/magnetic + aurora/film-grain/site-atmosphere styles. (7) src/server.ts - reverted img-src to 'self' data:' (grep confirmed no createObjectURL/toBlob/new Blob/new Worker in client code); KEPT worker-src 'self' blob:' for the Vite dev client/devtools; rewrote CSP comments to drop three/@react-three/drei/draco references and describe the same-origin video/CSS/lenis reality. Verification: git grep for @react-three/components/three/HeroScene/three imports = 0 matches; ImmersiveHero/HeroCanvas/ClientCanvas = 0; home-hero-canvas/immersive-canvas-layer/immersive-hero-canvas/immersive-hero-overlay/z-canvas = 0. LOCKFILE CAVEAT: package-lock.json was NOT touched (already stale, cannot be regenerated in this INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox with no npm registry access); it must be regenerated on a networked machine. Deploy (nixpacks.toml) and CI both use `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` which reconciles it, so this does not break those paths. typecheck/lint/test/build could NOT be run in-sandbox (no tool binaries, network firewalled); validated by reasoning + git grep dead-reference checks.
